{{Short description|Algebraic structure generalizing Boolean rings}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''clean ring''' is a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] in which every element can be written as the sum of a [[unit (ring theory)|unit]] and an [[idempotent element (ring theory)|idempotent]]. A ring is a [[local ring]] if and only if it is clean and has no idempotents other than 0 and&nbsp;1. The [[endomorphism ring]] of a [[continuous module]] is a clean ring.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Continuous modules are clean|last1=Camillo|first1=V.P.|last2=Khurana|first2=D.|last3=Lam|first3=T.Y.|author-link3=Tsit Yuen Lam|last4=Nicholson|first4=W.K.|last5=Zhou|first5=Y.|journal=Journal of Algebra|doi=10.1016/j.jalgebra.2006.06.032|volume=304|issue=1|pages=94–111|date=October 2006|doi-access=free}}</ref> Every clean ring is an [[exchange ring]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Nicholson, W. K.|volume=229|year=1977|pages=269-278|doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1977-0439876-2|MR=0439876|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1977-229-00/S0002-9947-1977-0439876-2/S0002-9947-1977-0439876-2.pdf|title=Lifting idempotents and exchange rings|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|access-date=9 June 2016}}</ref> A [[matrix ring]] over a clean ring is itself clean.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Communications in Algebra|volume=29|issue=6|doi=10.1081/AGB-100002409|last1=Hana|first1=Juncheol|last2=Nicholson|first2=W. K.|title=Extensions of Clean Rings|pages=2589–2595|year = 2001|s2cid=122957451}}</ref> Every [[Boolean ring]] is trivially a clean ring, since every element is idempotent.
